blinding_guess.why: The most salient candidate is field:std_msgs/Header.stamp: every goal PoseStamped the panel builds leaves header.stamp at its default zero value because both assignments are commented out (nav2_panel.cpp:713, 951). Whether that counts as a defect depends on the consumer. The provided action:/compute_path_to_pose is simply absent from this RViz plugin package, which looks like an element-assignment question rather than a code defect.

notes: msg_type naming: the action type is written in the ROS 2 fully qualified form nav2_msgs/action/NavigateToPose; message types follow the packet's pkg/Type form. action:/navigate_to_pose: the client is created on a separate rclcpp::Node (name remapped to navigation_dialog_action_client, no namespace set, nav2_panel.cpp:453-455) with the relative name navigate_to_pose, so it resolves to /navigate_to_pose. In addition the panel subscribes on the RViz node to navigate_to_pose/_action/feedback and navigate_to_pose/_action/status with rclcpp::SystemDefaultsQoS() (nav2_panel.cpp:786-788, 819-821), whose reliability and durability are RMW SYSTEM_DEFAULT, i.e. chosen by the RMW implementation, not by the snapshot. The action client's own status topic defaults to TRANSIENT_LOCAL; the recorded durability (volatile) is that of the goal/result/cancel services and the feedback topic. Frames: the NavigateToPose goal frame is not hard-coded; onNewGoal sets pose.header.frame_id from the RViz fixed frame supplied at run time by GoalTool (goal_tool.cpp:48 context_->getFixedFrame(); nav2_panel.cpp:952), so ports[0].frame, ports[1].frame and ports[3].frame are null. Waypoints loaded from file get the hard-coded frame "map" (convert_to_msg, nav2_panel.cpp:712) and are sent to follow_waypoints / navigate_through_poses, not navigate_to_pose. An optional initial waypoint copies its whole header from a TF lookup (nav2_panel.cpp:1056-1068). Stamp: header.stamp is never assigned for goals; both assignments are commented out with the remark that the client node does not respect sim time (nav2_panel.cpp:713, 951), so goals carry a zero stamp. Marker headers on topic waypoints copy the pose headers (nav2_panel.cpp:1379, 1397, 1415). QoS for the field and msg ports is null: those elements are not endpoints of their own; they travel inside action goals (goal service, rcl_action default RELIABLE/VOLATILE) and inside the MarkerArray on topic waypoints (rclcpp::QoS(1).transient_local(), nav2_panel.cpp:591-593). Dependency definitions (std_msgs/Header.msg, geometry_msgs/PoseStamped.msg, geometry_msgs/Pose.msg) were fetched from ros2/common_interfaces at tag 4.2.3 and at ref humble; the files were byte-identical. NavigateToPose.action was taken from the snapshot's own nav2_msgs (manifest 1.2.0). The package manifest version is 1.2.0 while the packet gives ros_distro humble; recorded as found. Other interfaces the code consumes but which are not packet elements: actions follow_waypoints and navigate_through_poses, lifecycle manager clients for lifecycle_manager_navigation and lifecycle_manager_localization (nav2_panel.cpp:457-460), parameter base_frame declared on the RViz node with default base_footprint (nav2_panel.cpp:781).
